QUOTE: "\"Try Again\" calls `retryFailedPost`, which rebuilds the API post with `failed: false`... then calls `client.createPost` once more." and "On failure, it sets `failed: true` again. The same three error IDs remove the post instead."
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer says `retryFailedPost` makes one more `createPost` call, marks the post failed again on error, and removes it for the same three errors. It does not mention a loop or backoff explicitly. The "once more" wording and the "zero automatic retries" framing cover the one-attempt claim.
